[Introduction]

Hi, I’m Klevis. I’m currently focusing on formal methods and understanding how to build better abstractions for robust, fault-tolerant systems. As LLMs generate more and more code, how do we specify precisely what we want to build, and how do we verify that the generated code satisfies that specification?

Software Formal Verification Researcher | December 2024 – January 2026 | BME, Budapest

I worked on improving the efficiency and capabilities of the ⁨Theta⁩ software verification framework at ⁨FTSRG, BME⁩, under the supervision of ⁨Zsófia Ádám⁩. In collaboration with PhD researchers and other contributors, I developed methods for transferring partial results between verification algorithms and introduced a new stopping heuristic. This research won first place in the software section of the TDK conference and formed the basis of my bachelor’s thesis. I also implemented support for ⁨Software Witness 2.0⁩ using the product automaton of XCFAs and worked on optimizing IMC in Theta. I evaluated these contributions on ⁨Theta BenchCloud⁩ using ⁨SV-Benchmarks⁩ and ⁨BenchExec⁩ to obtain reproducible performance measurements.
